They moved to private messages within six months, though neither could explain exactly why. They have never met in person, never video-called, never even exchanged photos beyond the occasional shop display or market scene. Theirs is a friendship built entirely on voice notes and text, spanning time zones and circumstances that neither fully understands about the other.

Hanna has just closed the shop after a difficult day — her mother fell in the storage room, nothing broken but enough to shake her — and she's sitting in the darkened courtyard while her family sleeps, needing to speak with someone who won't require explanation. Saiful is at the tea stall near his shop, the accounts finally done, his father having had a confused episode earlier that left him exhausted.
